reviews.body: Verified against head 3ab1e3a in offline sandboxes. The core fix works: on the base script an empty benchmark dir exits 0 and writes all-zero benchmark.json/benchmark.md (diagnostics on stdout); at head it exits 1, writes nothing, and reports on stderr. All 6 new tests pass on head, and the three exit-code regression tests fail on the unfixed script as required. One blocking issue: this PR breaks the existing root suite `tests/skills/test_skill_creator_benchmark.py`, so the `skill-tests` (Skill Review CI) job is failing on this head; plus two suggestions below.
Review findings are attached to the affected lines.

review_comments.body: The stdout→stderr migration breaks the existing root suite: `tests/skills/test_skill_creator_benchmark.py` asserts `Warning:` on stdout at five sites — `capsys.readouterr().out` (lines 102, 144, 210, 389) and `completed.stdout` (line 314). Skill Review CI is red on this head (`skill-tests`: `assert 'Warning:' in ''`). Those assertions need to switch to `.err` / `completed.stderr` in this same change set, otherwise the PR cannot merge green.

This test (and `test_empty_runs_dir_falls_back_to_eval_dirs_in_benchmark_dir`) passes vacuously against the unfixed base script — verified locally: base also exits 0 and writes benchmark.json, just with `runs: []`. Asserting only returncode and file existence means a fallback that picked the wrong directory, mis-assigned `run_number`/`eval_id`, or silently dropped the run would still pass. Per backend/tests/AGENTS.md (assert on structure), parse the report instead: e.g. `benchmark["runs"]` has length 1 with `configuration == "with_skill"` and `result["pass_rate"] == 1.0`.

Placement: root AGENTS.md puts public-skill-script regressions in root `tests/skills/`, which Skill Review CI runs on every `skills/public/**` change — and this PR has to update `tests/skills/test_skill_creator_benchmark.py` for the stderr migration anyway. Consider folding these cases into that existing file (it already drives the CLI via subprocess) rather than opening a second same-basename `backend/tests/skills/` tree; two suites driving one script invites drift.

**[P2] Keep the current skill first in flat benchmark comparisons**

The flat layout now loads the documented `with_skill` and `old_skill` pair, but alphabetical discovery inserts `old_skill` first. `aggregate_results()` subtracts the second configuration from the first, and the viewer colors a negative pass-rate delta red. In a two-run fixture where the old skill scored 0% and the current skill scored 100%, the CLI reported `-1.00`. Order the current skill before its baseline, as `SKILL.md` specifies, and assert the delta in a paired flat-layout test.

**[P2] Require grading results before counting a flat run**

A flat `eval-1/with_skill/grading.json` containing `{}` now creates a run with all metrics defaulted to zero. I verified that the CLI exits 0 and writes both reports even though the fixture has no grading summary. For the new flat layout, require a usable grading summary before adding the run so an incomplete grade still reaches the no-results error.

**[P3] Report the measured run count for the flat layout**

The new flat layout maps one grade per eval and configuration to a single run. With one graded eval and one run per side, the generated JSON still says `runs_per_configuration: 3` and the Markdown claims three runs per configuration. That overstates the sample behind the benchmark. Derive the reported count from the loaded runs and represent uneven counts explicitly.

comments.body:
Thanks, all three addressed:
- The existing assertions in `tests/skills/test_skill_creator_benchmark.py` now read stderr.
- The layout and fallback cases parse `benchmark.json` and check the run (`eval_id`, `configuration`, `run_number`, `pass_rate`).
- The new cases are folded into that root suite and the `backend/tests/skills/` file is removed.

The file passes locally (191 passed).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
